title: Chanda Mama Counts the Stars
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and assessment scenes instead of copying textbook prose.

levels.title: A sky too full to count
levels.teaching_goal: Connect repeated counting, changing stars, and Chanda Mama's frustration to the poem's central problem.

guided_check.teaching_block: A central problem is larger than one detail. Chanda Mama starts counting, loses his place, and begins again because the sky seems endlessly full.
guided_check.passage: Chanda Mama points from one bright speck to the next. A cloud passes, more stars appear, and he forgets his number.
options: He cannot finish counting the stars.
accepted_answers: He cannot finish counting the stars.
he cannot finish counting the stars

bridge.teaching_block: Break the problem into goal and obstacle. Goal: count every star. Obstacle: there are too many and the view keeps changing.
bridge.passage: He reaches ninety, a cloud moves away, and a new patch of stars appears.
bridge.prompt: Which detail makes the count difficult?
options: a new patch of stars appears
accepted_answers: a new patch of stars appears

masterclass.teaching_block: Do not confuse Chanda Mama's feeling with his problem. Sadness is a result; the unfinished star count is the problem.
masterclass.passage: He sighs and lowers his counting beads after losing his place again.
masterclass.prompt: Which answer names the problem, not only the feeling?
options: He repeatedly loses track of the countless stars.
accepted_answers: He repeatedly loses track of the countless stars.
he repeatedly loses track of the countless stars

independent_check.teaching_block: Read a fresh sky scene and explain its central problem.
independent_check.passage: Mira marks each star she sees on a slate. Mist covers one side of the sky, then clears to reveal many more lights than before.
independent_check.prompt: What prevents Mira from completing an accurate count?

concept_slots.description: Mention counting or marking the stars.
Mention the changing view or newly visible stars.
State that the count cannot be completed or trusted.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply the idea of a changing count to a busy ground scene.
transfer_check.passage: At a fair gate, Arjun counts visitors. People enter through one side while others leave through another.
transfer_check.prompt: Explain why Arjun's total keeps changing.

concept_slots.description: Mention people entering.
Mention people leaving.
Explain that the group is not staying the same.

levels.title: Understand the Sun's kind answer
levels.teaching_goal: Infer how the Sun comforts Chanda Mama by changing the task from exact counting to appreciating many bright children.

guided_check.teaching_block: A comforting answer may not solve the exact task. The Sun helps Chanda Mama stop worrying by comparing the many stars to the many children below.
guided_check.passage: Chanda Mama says, 'I can never finish.' The Sun replies, 'Think of every star as one smiling child. You do not need one final number to value them.'
guided_check.prompt: Why does the Sun make this comparison?
options: to help Chanda Mama feel better
accepted_answers: to help Chanda Mama feel better

bridge.teaching_block: Find feeling, action, result. Chanda Mama is upset; the Sun offers a warm idea; he smiles again.
bridge.passage: The Sun reminds him that some wonderful things can be enjoyed without an exact total.
bridge.prompt: What result does the Sun want?

masterclass.teaching_block: A misconception is that help must finish the counting. The Sun's help is emotional: it gives a kinder way to think about the stars.
masterclass.passage: The count is still unfinished, but Chanda Mama lifts his face and smiles.

independent_check.teaching_block: Infer the reason in a new conversation.
independent_check.passage: Noor is upset because she cannot name every bird in a huge flock. Her grandfather says, 'You noticed how beautifully they move together. That matters too.'
independent_check.prompt: Why do the grandfather's words help Noor?

concept_slots.description: Mention that Noor cannot name every bird.
Mention noticing or enjoying the flock.
Explain that exact naming is not required.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Give a kind reason in a school context.
transfer_check.passage: Veer cannot colour every leaf on a large class mural before the bell. His team has already completed a bright forest together.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one sentence that could reassure Veer and explain why.

concept_slots.description: Say the shared mural or effort already matters.
Mention that every leaf need not be finished by Veer alone.
any_of: does not need to do all

concept_slots.description: Use a supportive tone.

levels.title: Words for an endless sky
levels.teaching_goal: Use context to understand countless, glimmer, and weary in moon-and-star scenes.

guided_check.teaching_block: The suffix -less can mean without. Countless stars are so many that they seem without a count.
guided_check.passage: Countless lights cover the sky; Chanda Mama cannot reach a final number.

bridge.teaching_block: A glimmer is a small or faint light. Use the clue 'tiny light' to find the meaning.
bridge.passage: One glimmer appears between two dark clouds.

masterclass.teaching_block: Weary means tired, not sad. A person may feel both, but the clue repeated work points to tiredness.
masterclass.passage: After counting for hours, Chanda Mama's eyes droop and his hand feels heavy.

independent_check.teaching_block: Use the clue in the unseen sentence.
independent_check.passage: A faint star was barely visible through the thin cloud.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use the word in a different setting.
transfer_check.passage: Countless ants streamed around the fallen sugar cube.

levels.title: Name, action, and description
levels.teaching_goal: Use noun, verb, and adjective roles to build clear moon-and-star sentences.

guided_check.teaching_block: In 'The round moon glows,' moon is a noun, glows is a verb, and round is an adjective.
guided_check.prompt: Which word tells what the silver stars do?

bridge.teaching_block: Find the thing first, then its describing word.
bridge.passage: A curved moon hangs above the roof.

masterclass.teaching_block: Position does not decide word type. In 'Stars twinkle brightly,' stars name things and twinkle shows action.
masterclass.prompt: Which pair is noun then verb?

independent_check.prompt: Write the naming word for the sky object.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Build a sentence in an ocean setting.
transfer_check.passage: A white sail moves across calm water.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one complete sentence with a noun, an action verb, and an adjective.

concept_slots.description: Name a sail, boat, or water.
Use an action or state verb.
Use a fitting describing word.

levels.title: Send Chanda Mama courage
levels.focus: write a friendly message and summary
levels.teaching_goal: Write a short supportive message that recognizes Chanda Mama's problem and offers a helpful thought.

guided_check.teaching_block: A friendly message has a greeting, a clear supportive thought, and a sign-off. Example: 'Dear Chanda Mama, do not worry about one final count. Your careful effort helps us notice the beautiful sky. From, Ria.'
guided_check.passage: Chanda Mama has lost count again and feels discouraged.
guided_check.prompt: Which message opening is warm and specific?
options: Dear Chanda Mama, your patient counting helps everyone notice the stars.
accepted_answers: Dear Chanda Mama, your patient counting helps everyone notice the stars.
dear Chanda Mama, your patient counting helps everyone notice the stars

bridge.teaching_block: Build the middle from two parts: notice the difficulty + offer encouragement.
bridge.passage: Difficulty: the stars are too many. Encouragement: enjoy their light without worrying about a final number.
options: Even if the stars are too many to count, you can enjoy their light.
accepted_answers: Even if the stars are too many to count, you can enjoy their light.
even if the stars are too many to count, you can enjoy their light

masterclass.teaching_block: A friendly message is not a command with no care. It should show understanding before giving advice.
masterclass.passage: Chanda Mama is weary after another unfinished count.
masterclass.prompt: Which message is supportive rather than bossy?
options: You worked hard; rest now and try again only if you wish.
accepted_answers: You worked hard; rest now and try again only if you wish.
you worked hard; rest now and try again only if you wish

independent_check.passage: Chanda Mama worries that an unfinished count means his work has no value.
